To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of non uniformly spaced phase screens along the propagation distance with an effective structure constant for the screen chosen to minimize the contribution to the receiver scintillation provides better agreement with the analytic results.

we developed a numerical method to model the propagation of optical beams through turbulence using a non uniformly spaced phase screens with modified Hufnagle-Valley turbulence profile and that we showed that our model provides a good agreement with the analytical results for scintillation index.

the irradiance and the phase statistics for a beam propagating through atmospheric turbulence can be modeled using a series of thin screens with a modified von Karman phase statistics and a non uniform spacing of the screens along the optical path.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the propagation of optical beams through the atmospheric turbulence.
the development of a numerical model that is capable of predicting the performance of a free space optical communication link in the presence of atmospheric turbulence.
the propagation of optical waves in atmospheric turbulence and its application to the design of free space optical communications systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results presented herein demonstrate that the non uniformly spaced screen approach is an effective method to simulate beam propagation through atmospheric turbulence.
the non-uniformly spaced screen model provides a more realistic model for the atmospheric turbulence than the uniformly spaced screen model.
the non uniform screen method is a flexible and effective tool that can be used to model the effects of atmospheric propagation in free space optical communication applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a non uniform screen spacing with an altitude dependent structure constant can be used to accurately model atmospheric turbulence in a wave optical simulation.
a non uniform distribution of phase screens is a viable alternative to the standard layered model and can provide a more accurate model for the propagation of optical beams in atmospheric turbulence.

a more realistic simulation of the propagation of optical waves through turbulence can be obtained by using a non uniformly distributed phase screen model with an altitude dependent structure constant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the non uniformly spaced screen model can be used to improve the agreement with the analytical results for the irradiance variance, phase variance, and the probability of fade.

the scintillation index can be minimized in the receiver plane using a non uniform screen spacing with the effective value of C _{n} ^{2} for each screen chosen such that the total contribution of each screen to the scintillating irradiance is minimized.
a non uniform distribution of screens is more effective than a uniformly distributed model in terms of minimizing the scintillation at the receiver plane.
